instructions.plastic: Empty, rinse and dry it, then put it in the recycling bin. Leave caps on.
instructions.glass: Rinse the glass and place it in the recycling bin. Do not break it first.
instructions.metal: Rinse cans and foil, then recycle. Crush cans to save space.
instructions.cardboard: Flatten the cardboard and keep it dry before recycling.
instructions.paper: Keep paper clean and dry, then recycle. No greasy or wet paper.
instructions.biological: Put food scraps in the compost or green/organic bin.
instructions.vegetation: Add garden and plant waste to the compost or green bin.
instructions.battery: Do NOT bin batteries. Drop them at a battery / e-waste collection point.
instructions.trash: This goes in the general landfill bin.
instructions.clothes: Reuse or donate if wearable; otherwise textile-recycle or landfill.
instructions.shoes: Donate wearable shoes; otherwise place in the general waste bin.

common_mistakes.plastic: People leave food residue inside, which contaminates a whole batch.
common_mistakes.glass: Broken glass and drinking glasses/Pyrex are often not accepted - check locally.
common_mistakes.metal: Small foil balls and bottle caps are frequently missed by sorters.
common_mistakes.cardboard: Greasy pizza boxes are not recyclable - tear off clean parts only.
common_mistakes.paper: Shredded paper and laminated paper usually cannot be recycled.
common_mistakes.biological: Compostable plastics are often mistaken for real compost - they are not.
common_mistakes.vegetation: Treated or painted wood should not go in green waste.
common_mistakes.battery: Throwing batteries in normal bins is a fire hazard and illegal in many places.
common_mistakes.trash: Many "trash" items are actually recyclable - double-check first.
common_mistakes.clothes: Wet or mouldy textiles ruin whole donation bags.
common_mistakes.shoes: Odd single shoes still have recycling value - keep pairs together.
